title: Gestalt Principles
summary: Gestalt principles describe how people perceive grouping and relationships; VIS-008 owns the definitions, EVAL-005 applies them.

MUST.text: Use proximity to group labels and controls; similarity for same-function elements.
Define and apply: proximity, similarity, continuity, closure, figure-ground, common region, common fate.
Use a boundary (card, divider, background) when proximity alone is ambiguous.

SHOULD.text: Keep within-group gap clearly smaller than between-group gap (e.g., <=8px inside, >=24px between).
Style elements with the same behavior identically; differentiate distinct roles.
Verify perceived groups against semantic relationships and task flow.

AVOID.text: Grouping unrelated controls because they share a card.
Relying on proximity when responsive reflow breaks it.

DECIDE.decision: Group by task, not layout convenience

EXAMPLE.good: "Field label, input and error form one perceived group; submit separate."
EXAMPLE.bad: "Card groups submit button with unrelated settings."

FAILURE_MODES: Visual grouping can imply false hierarchy; verify with task scanning.
Consistent styling across different behaviors causes misclicks.
Responsive reflow can break grouping; re-check at narrow widths.
Proximity without boundaries becomes ambiguous in dense layouts.
